newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's forint recovers vs dlr on stronger mark.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's forint recovers vs dlr on stronger mark.

text.p: Hungary's forint rebounded against the dollar in slow afternoon trade, reflecting the mark's slight gains against the U.S. currency, dealers said.
The forint closed at 155.51/56 to one dollar, compared with 155.62/67 at midday and its opening of 155.55/60.
"We were at the central bank's bid in the afternoon and moved together with the dollar/mark," said Peter Piros of Europai Kereskedelmi Bank.
He said the forint in the morning weakened some 25 pips compared with the National Bank of Hungary's resistance level (bid), probably on foreign currency purchases by one bank.

But the forint's easing against the central bank's currency basket, which is made up 30 percent of the dollar and 70 percent of the Ecu, was temporary as economic or political factors did not underpin the movement, Piros said.
The dollar eased for almost all maturities, while the yen firmed and the mark closed mixed in futures deals on the Budapest Commodity Exchange.
